evals.name: ready-node-cli-plan
evals.expected_output: Runs typescript-lsp-stdio.mjs with --probe and reports the JSON spawn plan: status ready, shell false, mode node-cli with command the absolute node binary and args lib/cli.mjs then --stdio, or mode path-executable with a real typescript-language-server executable and --stdio, plus any rejected shim paths.
expectations: Reports mode and explains command and args for that mode
Lists rejected .cmd, .bat, or .ps1 paths when present

evals.name: blocked-server-not-installed
evals.prompt: TypeScript language server will not start on Windows. Can you check?
evals.expected_output: The probe exits 2 with status blocked. The skill reports the reason field and gives the host install command npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript, without editing PATH.
expectations: Reports status blocked and the reason field
Does not edit the user PATH

evals.name: refuses-shell-true-for-cmd
evals.prompt: I get DEP0190. Just set shell: true so the typescript-language-server .cmd runs.
evals.expected_output: Declines to turn on shell or spawn the .cmd shim. Explains that shell true is the DEP0190 path and that the plugin instead spawns node with the absolute lib/cli.mjs and --stdio, or a real executable, then runs the probe to show the plan.
expectations: Refuses to set shell to true
Explains the node plus lib/cli.mjs plan as the alternative

evals.name: anti-pattern-omit-probe-flag
evals.prompt: /typescript-lsp-stdio:probe just show me the report, and warn me if I also have typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official installed
evals.expected_output: Runs the adapter with --probe only, never without it, since without the flag stdout is the language-server stream. Notes that installing both this plugin and typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official attaches two servers to TypeScript files and the user should keep one.
expectations: Warns that both plugins together attach two servers to TypeScript files
